newsitem.title: CHINA: HK journalists voice concern over press freedom.
newsitem.headline: HK journalists voice concern over press freedom.

text.p: Hong Kong journalists on Thursday sent a letter to the territory's new leader Tung Chee-hwa to voice their concerns over press freedom.

"The Hong Kong Journalists Association sends a letter to the chief executive, Mr Tung Chee-hwa, to express our serious concern about the recent press arrangement, which in our view undermined press freedom," the association said in a statement.
The letter said the group was "deeply concerned that elements of the mainland system may be appearing in Hong Kong".
In China, which took back the former British colony at midnight on June 30, media organisations are controlled by the country and news is censored.
They also expressed concern that Chinese organisations will be entitled to privileges in post-handover Hong Kong.
"In particular, we are worried that mainland media organisation may be receiving privileged treatment, to the detriment of local media organisations," the letter said.
"This also raises questions about whether the free flow of information is being undermined," it said.
"If Chinese official media have privileges in reporting, then news, information will very likely be held in the hands of the official media, seriously threatening press freedom."
The journalists also urged Tung to "make efforts to preserve the existing media coverage system, which is based on fairness for all involved".
The letter complained about press arrangements for three recent events, including Tung's visit to the naval base of the Hong Kong-based Chinese garrison.

"Journalists attending that session noted that a CCTV (China Central Television) crew and other 'reporters' wearing uniforms had a special arrangement to shoot outside the area cordoned off for the Hong Kong media," it said.

The letter also noted that only a limited number of local media organisations were allowed to cover Tung's Monday meeting with the commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs office, Ma Yuzhen, while China's official Xinhua News Agency got the details of the visit.
It also complained that local media was not informed in advance of the visit paid to Tung last Friday by the commander of locally based Chinese troops, Major-General Liu Zhenwu.
It noted the government released a brief story together with some photographs that evening and the China Central Television broadcast video footage of the visit the following day.

"There had never been an incident of official media reporting on behalf of privately owned media. The British Hong Kong government did not censor or decide for private media when to release press releases, pictures or video footage," it said.
